name: buzzsearch-mcp

tools.name: search
tools.description: Search the web for user-generated content: what real people say about a product, problem or audience in comments on Reddit, YouTube, TikTok and Facebook groups. Runs a full live search: finds threads and videos across the web, reads their comments, extracts verbatim quotes and writes a cited answer. A query that contains a TikTok video, creator profile or hashtag link, a bare creator @handle (TikTok unless the query says YouTube), a YouTube video or channel link, a Reddit thread or subreddit link, or a Facebook group post link reads that link's own comments directly (add a question after the link to also search the topic). A query that is a pasted list of comments is analyzed directly with no web search. A search usually takes one to three minutes, longer than one call can wait: it waits up to `wait_seconds` and returns the answer with the top quotes when done, otherwise the exact `get_search` call to make next; keep calling `get_search` until the status is completed. Costs credits from the BuzzSearch balance at the API rate; the exact charge is reported on completion as `credits_charged` with `balance_after`. When the balance cannot cover a search the call fails with INSUFFICIENT_CREDITS and a top-up link: tell the user and share the link. Check `list_searches` first: a prior search on the same topic can be reread for free.

query.description: The research question, e.g. 'what do people hate about robot vacuums'.

depth.description: quick (about a minute), deep (about three), exhaustive (longest, most comments).

sources.description: Default: reddit, youtube, tiktok. Add facebook for group discussions.

time_range.description: How recent the posts and comments should be. Default: any time.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait server-side for completion before returning (0 to 55). Call again to resume.

annotations.title: Search UGC and social comments across the web

tools.name: get_search
tools.description: Read a search's status, cited answer, coverage counts and top quotes. Free. Pass `turn_id` to read a specific follow-up answer, otherwise the latest turn is returned. A finished search returns at once; a running one is held open for up to 55s and returns as soon as it finishes, so call it again until status is "completed".

search_id.description: The search id returned by `search` or `list_searches`.

turn_id.description: A turn id from `search`, `ask` or `generate_hooks`. Default: the latest turn.

tools.name: get_quotes
tools.description: Verbatim customer quotes extracted by a search, filtered and paged. Free. Each quote carries a stable id, the source url, a dimension (emotional_painpoints, recurring_painpoints, desired_outcomes, failed_solutions, objections, customer_lingo), an engagement score and an emotional intensity (1 to 5). For ad copy, pull emotional_painpoints and customer_lingo sorted by intensity.

search_id.description: The search id returned by `search` or `list_searches`.

contains.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the quote text.

tools.name: get_sources
tools.description: The threads and videos a search read, with engagement, comment counts and how many quotes each produced. Free. Use it to cite a thread or pick which source's raw comments to pull.

search_id.description: The search id returned by `search` or `list_searches`.

tools.name: get_comments
tools.description: The raw comment bodies behind a completed search, grouped by thread or video, filtered and paged. Free. A search reads hundreds to thousands of comments, so filter by source, a substring, or a minimum score, and page with limit and offset.

search_id.description: The search id returned by `search` or `list_searches`.

contains.description: Case-insensitive substring filter on the comment body.

tools.name: ask
tools.description: Ask a new question over a completed search's corpus and get a cited answer, without searching again. Costs less than a new search: only the answer is metered at the API rate. Good for 'what do they say about price', 'summarize the objections', 'which phrases do they use for the problem'. Works on searches started through the API or MCP.

search_id.description: The search id returned by `search` or `list_searches`.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait server-side for completion before returning (0 to 55). Call again to resume.

tools.name: generate_hooks
tools.description: Write ad hooks grounded in a completed search's quotes, using BuzzSearch's hook writer: each hook opens with a callout lifted from real comments and carries a loop or promise. Metered at the API rate, no new search. Works on searches started through the API or MCP. Give an `angle` to steer (a product, a persona, a platform).

search_id.description: The search id returned by `search` or `list_searches`.

angle.description: Optional steer, e.g. 'TikTok UGC for a $40 posture corrector'.

wait_seconds.description: Seconds to wait server-side for completion before returning (0 to 55). Call again to resume.

tools.name: list_searches
tools.description: Recent searches by the signed-in user, newest first, including ones run in the BuzzSearch app. Free. Reread a past search with get_search or get_quotes instead of paying for a new one on the same topic.

contains.description: Case-insensitive filter on the search query.

channel.description: api = started via API or MCP, web = run in the app.

tools.name: get_balance
tools.description: The user's BuzzSearch credit balance, with a link to top up. Searches draw from it at the API rate.

instructions:
BuzzSearch researches what real people say in Reddit, YouTube, TikTok and Facebook group comments and returns verbatim quotes with source links. Use it for customer pains, desires, objections, product feedback, audience language and ad angles.

What `search` accepts: a research question; a TikTok video, profile or hashtag link, a creator @handle, a YouTube video or channel link, a Reddit thread or subreddit link, or a Facebook group post link (reads that link's comments; add a question after it to also search the topic); or a pasted list of comments (analyzed directly). Options: depth quick (default), deep or exhaustive; sources; time_range for recent posts only.

Workflow: call list_searches first and reuse a completed search on the same topic. Otherwise call search. A search takes one to three minutes: when it returns before completion, call get_search with the given search_id and turn_id until status is completed, then answer.

After a search completes, none of these search again: get_quotes (verbatim quotes filtered by dimension, source, intensity or text), get_sources (threads and videos read), get_comments (raw comment bodies), ask (a follow-up question over the same corpus), generate_hooks (ad hooks grounded in the quotes).

Quote customers verbatim and cite each quote's url. When a reply includes sources_url, give it to the user: it opens every comment and source the search read, searchable and filterable.
